body:
CONFIRMED BY RUNNING IT (2026-07-21). `test/gateway/promote-survival-probe.test.ts` reproduces it. Found during the T38 fallout sweep - same family, DIFFERENT REMEDY, which is why it is its own ticket.

WHAT HAPPENS. `promoteImpl` (src/gateway/adopt.ts) gates on presence:

    const src = source.reactor.get(deltaId);
    if (src === undefined) throw new Error(`nothing to promote: ...`);

`reactor.get` says the delta EXISTS in the pool. It says nothing about whether it SURVIVES there - whether something in the pool struck it. Meanwhile `promotionRefusal` correctly refuses to promote a NEGATION ('a retraction is the operator's own §14 act, never an adopted output').

Each rule is right alone; together they leave a hole. The retraction cannot cross, but its target can. So a sandboxed app that produces an interpretation and then WITHDRAWS it leaves an output the operator can still adopt - and promotion RE-SIGNS, so the withdrawn claim enters the primary in the OPERATOR'S OWN VOICE with full force. The record then shows the operator asserting something its author had already taken back, with a `loam.adoption` trail that makes it look properly sourced.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN T38. T38's seeding edge gave a POOL a wrong reading of the primary - bad, but contained behind glass and dropped with the pool. This puts a resurrected claim into CANONICAL history under the operator's signature, where §11 erasure is the only way back out. Promotion is the one door out of the quarantine (§24.9's 'promotion is the only crossing'), so it is exactly the door that must not pass something the pool had already struck.

FIX (recommendation): `promoteImpl` refuses a source delta that does not SURVIVE in the source. Reuse the pool's own negation reading rather than inventing a second notion of survival - whatever `lawfulNegated`/the reactor already answers for 'is this struck', ask that. The refusal must NAME the retraction (the codebase's refusals say why), and it belongs beside the existing `promotionRefusal` checks so the whole promotion gate reads in one place.

Decide one thing explicitly and write it into §24.3: does a LATER retraction in the pool retroactively affect an ALREADY-adopted delta? Recommendation: NO, and say so - the adoption was a lawful operator act at the time, the adopted delta is the operator's own claim now, and withdrawing it is the operator's own §14 retraction rather than an echo of the pool's. Anything else would make canonical history mutable by a sandbox, which is the property §24 exists to deny. But it must be STATED, because the alternative reading is defensible and silence would leave it to whoever implements next.

RAILS:
- The probe: a pool output struck inside the pool cannot be promoted; the refusal names the retraction.
- TRANSITIVE: strike, then counter-strike (which revives), and promotion SUCCEEDS again - survival is the live reading, not 'was ever negated'.
- An already-adopted delta is unaffected by a retraction landing in the pool afterwards (the decision above, railed).
- Unchanged: every existing promotion path stays green - `test/gateway/promotion.test.ts` with no assertion softened, idempotence and the erasure interaction (#111) intact.

CARE: capability + federation surface, and it changes what enters canonical history -> Myk's merge (P6).

DECIDED AT BUILD (2026-07-25) — REFUSE, not carry, and the property that decides it is DOOR vs STANDING PASS rather than law-vs-fact.

T33 refuses (spec criterion 25) and T58's translate edge carries, and the two are not in tension: a door knows survival BEFORE anything is signed, so its honest act is to not sign; `translate` is not a door — its rendering has already LANDED by the time the source is struck, and its audience is a peer running none of Loam's reader rules, so only a delta can suppress. Promotion is a door.

Carrying at THIS door would also be mechanically worse than refusing. Promotion is content-addressed on the source (§11 rung 2's inherited timestamp), so a copy landed already-struck would kill that adopted id forever: forgive the output in the pool, promote again, and the idempotence short-circuit hands back a delta no governed reader can see — an operation reporting a success it did not achieve (H7) at the one door §24.9 calls the only crossing. Refusal leaves nothing behind, and the reversibility is railed.

WHOSE STRIKE BINDS — TWO GROUNDS, because two different things can be wrong and only one is about the source store's reading. Round one shipped the author-scoped arm ALONE and two independent lenses confirmed that was a narrower rule wearing T33's clothes:

 1. THE SOURCE'S OWN GOVERNED READING — `dataStruck(source.reactor, source.operator)`, the mask a reader there resolves through. A pool shares the primary's operator seed (§24.1), so the operator's REJECT-THIS-OUTPUT strike inside their own pool is the §27 review gesture and must bind; under author-scoping alone it did not, and promotion overrode the operator's own rejection while the pool's own door served nothing for that fact. Same gap, second path: the seeding edge carries the primary's ground with its strikes, so a claim the operator retracted AT HOME could be promoted back out of their own quarantine and land live under a fresh id. `translate` already uses `dataStruck` for this same crossing because the pass filters DATA. An ungranted stranger still holds no veto; a GRANTEE's strike does bind, and that is the case that distinguishes this rule from operator-only.
 2. THE AUTHOR TOOK THEIR OWN WORD BACK — `lawfulNegated(source.reactor, src.claims.author)`, §27.8's rule transposed, scoped at every rung (a foreign negation-of-the-retraction cannot revive it). Invisible to (1) precisely in the ticket's headline case, since a quarantined app holds no grant. Not a claim about the source's reading but about whose sentence the operator is about to speak — so it has NO operator override by design: an output its author withdrew is unpromotable for good, and the escape hatch is to publish the claim as the operator's own §14 act rather than behind an adoption trail that would vouch for a withdrawn output. Both refusals name that remedy.

Survival is asked BEFORE the law/data classification, mirroring the blessing door: a struck delta is refused as struck, never by its kind (railed by its surviving twin, which refuses as a negation).

The later-retraction question is answered NO and railed: an adoption already made is untouched (the adopted delta is the operator's own claim, live and resolving), while a NEW promote() call is a new act judged against the pool as it stands and refuses.

ONE MORE RUNG FIXED (H7, found by the same review): the idempotence short-circuit returned `{ promoted }` over an adopted delta the operator had since struck in the PRIMARY — a success no governed reader could see, indistinguishable from the real thing. It refuses now and names the strike as the operator's to lift. An erased adoption still needs no branch: the delta is absent, the append meets its own tombstone, #111 unchanged.

STILL OPEN FOR §24.3 AT LANDING: the refusal narrows what promote() accepts, so a caller that used to succeed now throws. The substance is a repair (§28.4 already states that a filter narrowing a delta-set must not strand what struck it, and §24.9 makes promotion the one crossing), but the API narrowing is Myk's merge as this shard always said.
title: Promotion checks PRESENCE, not SURVIVAL - a retracted pool output is adopted in the operator's own voice
